classification.difficultyReason: Use the product rule and connect each given location to a zero of the derivative, using the exponent restrictions at 0 and 1.

content.prompt: Define the function $$f(x)=x^m(x-1)^n,$$ where $m$ and $n$ are integers greater than 1. Show that the graph is horizontal at $x=0,\ \frac{m}{m+n},\ 1$.

answer.short:
The graph has horizontal tangents at $x=0,\ \frac{m}{m+n},\ 1$.

$$f'(x)=x^{m-1}(x-1)^{n-1}[(m+n)x-m]$$

At each of these values a factor is zero.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=mx^{m-1}(x-1)^n+nx^m(x-1)^{n-1}\\f'(x)&=x^{m-1}(x-1)^{n-1}[m(x-1)+nx]\\f'(x)&=x^{m-1}(x-1)^{n-1}[(m+n)x-m]\end{align*}$$ Since $m-1>0$ and $n-1>0$, the first two factors give $f'(0)=0$ and $f'(1)=0$, respectively. The last factor is zero when $(m+n)x-m=0$, so $f'\left(\frac{m}{m+n}\right)=0$. The graph has a horizontal tangent at each of these three values.
